prize_parts.citation: For showing that small molecules can direct ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through bifunctional degraders and through the cereblon mechanism of thalidomide-type molecular glues

statement.case_for: My first-round choice stands. The chair asks whether B034 is one achievement or two, and I think it is one: chemically induced proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, which gives a measurable ternary complex, ubiquitin transfer and loss of the protein. A PROTAC builds that complex by design; a thalidomide-type glue reshapes cereblon so that it recruits neosubstrates. They differ in how the complex is assembled, not in what it does, and the glue arm explains why drugs used in patients for years work at all. That is also my answer on maturity: the cereblon arm has a long clinical record, and the bifunctional arm has been reproduced by many independent groups and is routinely used by biologists to remove a protein acutely. The criterion is a simple measurement, namely the protein disappears and the ternary complex can be quantified. My citation therefore credits Crews and Deshaies for the bifunctional principle and Handa for the molecular mechanism of glues, and it deliberately excludes optimisation work (Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures, Gray's later degraders) as refinements of an established principle, and Sakamoto and Kim's early PROTAC experiment as a proof of concept that I would acknowledge in the text but cannot fit under the cap.
statement.case_against: The three-person cap forces exclusions that others will call arbitrary, above all Ciulli, whose ligands and structural work made PROTACs a practical design problem, and Sakamoto, who co-authored the first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies. A citation spanning two arms can be read as a compromise, and Aili and Somfai both say so in their own terms. No bifunctional degrader is yet an approved drug, so for the PROTAC arm the clinical verdict is still pending. It also remains possible that the committee will regard this as chemical biology and pharmacology rather than chemistry, though I would say a designable reaction that removes a chosen protein is chemistry.

responses.point: Daniel would credit only Crews and Deshaies for the bifunctional degrader and treats Handa as optional, because the glue arm is a mechanism discovery and he would rather spend the place on a second achievement.
responses.response: I understand the logic but I do not think the glue arm is only a mechanism discovery. Handa's work identified the target through which existing drugs act and showed that a small molecule can remodel a ligase surface to recruit a new substrate, which is the same induced-proximity principle by a second route and the only part with a long patient record. Without it the citation rests entirely on a modality with no approved drug. I accept your point that Deshaies and Handa could be swapped, but I would rather keep all three than drop a pioneer of the PROTAC concept. On a second part, I remain uneasy about base editing: Somfai's remark that the innovation is protein engineering of a natural deaminase, and the closeness of the 2020 prize, weigh on me more than they do on you, so I will not add B012 to my configuration.

responses.point: Heiner asks me to separate what Crews and Deshaies discovered from later refinements, whether the lack of an approved PROTAC drug makes the verdict premature, and says one defensible citation could move him.
responses.response: Crews and Deshaies, with Sakamoto, showed in 2001 that a chimeric molecule can bring a protein to an E3 ligase and cause its ubiquitination and degradation; later work (VHL and cereblon ligands, cell-permeable all-small-molecule degraders, ternary-complex cooperativity) made it practical and is refinement of that principle. On timing, I agree an approved PROTAC would make the case easier, but the same mechanism is already demonstrated in patients through lenalidomide and pomalidomide, so the principle is not untested. My proposed citation is the one above, a single induced-proximity achievement with two entry routes. I would add that your own B011 is my first alternative, so I am not asking you to give up a mature candidate for an immature one, only to weigh both.

responses.point: Johan argues that sequencing by synthesis is mature and that the reversible-terminator chemistry is the decisive invention, and that B034 fails his test of realised consequences because no degrader is approved and credit is split over eight names.
responses.response: I agree that the Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and that the chemistry is real, so B011 is my first alternative and I would vote for it if B034 cannot be made to work. On his test, I would point out that thalidomide-class molecular glues have realised their consequences for many years; the open question is the PROTAC arm only. As for the eight names, the cap removes five of them by rule, and the remaining three correspond to two distinct experimental contributions, not to a split of one. My remaining doubt about B011 is the same one I raised earlier: whether the committee wants to reward the chemistry rather than the platform, and your citation wording, which names the reversible-terminator chemistry explicitly, handles that better than a generic sequencing citation would.

responses.point: Peter keeps B034 as first alternative but says a trio would honour one arm and leave the other, which is hard for a single citation, and would not put it ahead of two achievements with a long, stable record.
responses.response: The trio does not leave one arm out, since Crews and Deshaies stand for the bifunctional arm and Handa for the glue arm, so both are named in one sentence. I take the maturity point seriously for the PROTAC arm. Where I differ is that the Buchwald-Hartwig record is long and stable, but it sits next to the 2010 cross-coupling prize and Kosugi's earlier work, so it carries its own attribution and optics costs, and I would not call it free of them. I also note that your configuration needs Liu alone for base editing, and that pairing two parts with different logics is the compromise you yourself flagged.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a single induced-proximity citation covering both bifunctional degraders and molecular glues, or insist on separating them
Whether Crews, Deshaies and Handa is a defensible three given Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito are excluded
Whether the missing approval of a bifunctional degrader drug makes the PROTAC arm premature
Whether B011 (reversible-terminator chemistry) can be worded so that it rewards chemistry rather than the sequencing platform, since it is my main fallback
statement.conflict_note: No conflict. My work on dNTP pools and ribonucleotide reductase is unrelated to any shortlisted candidate, and I have no personal or institutional tie to any credited person. Nothing changed since round 1.
